articles.title: HUGE COMEBACK IN KC
articles.body: On the Monday Night Brawl, after being down 22-0, the Kansas City Chiefs come from behind and score 24 unanswered points against the Atlanta Falcons. Kansas City is now currently 4-1, and Atlanta is 3-2. The Chiefs are in playoff position, at 2nd in the AFC and 5th overall, and are sitting at the 5-seed in the AFC Playoff Picture. The Falcons are currently in 8th in the NFC and in 11th overall.

articles.title: Big Game for Indy
articles.body: The Rookie Wayne Chrebet made his first start for Indianapolis in their most recent game (a 21-10 victory) against the Minnesota Vikings. He played the whole game, scoring 3 TDs. The Colts are now 2-3 and are sitting in 8th in the AFC and 17th overall. The Vikings are now 0-5, sitting in last in the NFC and overall.

articles.title: Nothing But Flags Flying During Commanders/Titans Game
articles.body: Nothing but flags flew during the recent game between the Titans and Commanders. A total of eleven penalties were called (mostly personal fouls) in the bloodbath of that game. The Commanders had one illegal hit below the waist penalty, adding up to fifteen total penalty yards. The Titans had ten penalties called. Six late-hit out-of-bounds calls, one targeting, and three encroachment calls, adding up to one hundred ten penalty yards. One of the late hits resulted in Brian Robinson Jr., a third-year out of Alabama, getting injured. Two Titans players "personal fouled out" by committing three personal fouls: Bruce Matthews (Rookie) and DeAndre Hopkins (Second Year). One was disqualified due to targeting: Steve McNair, a third-year. All three players are facing one to three week suspensions, at the league's and team's discretion. As a result of three players getting disqualified, the Titans coach also had to go to the locker room for the last ninety seconds. The final score was Titans: 26, Commanders: 24.

articles.title: Brian Robinson Jr. on IR
articles.body: Brian Robinson Jr. left the recent game versus the Titans after a late hit. He has been placed on the 4-week IR for a mild concussion.

articles.title: Titans Players to Not be Suspended
articles.body: Two of the three Titans players will not receive suspensions. Bruce Matthews and DeAndre Hopkins will not be suspended due to their personal foul outs against Washington. Steve McNair's suspension for targeting has been confirmed for two weeks.

articles.title: TMFL OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT: MAJOR SCHEDULE UPDATE!
articles.body:
The TMFL has officially announced a major restructuring of the remaining 2026 regular-season schedule!

Following a league-wide schedule review, several changes have been implemented to improve competitive balance and make the race to the playoffs more exciting.

WHAT'S CHANGING?

DIVISIONAL RIVALRIES BEGIN IN WEEK 8!
All 96 divisional matchups have been redistributed across Weeks 8–18 instead of being concentrated in the final six weeks.

BYE WEEKS HAVE BEEN RESCHEDULED!
Bye weeks are now spread throughout Weeks 8–15. Every team will be in action during Weeks 16, 17, and 18, setting up a full slate of games for the final playoff push!

NEW STANDINGS TIEBREAKER!
Division winning percentage is now the first tiebreaker for teams with identical overall winning percentages, followed by the existing TMFL tiebreakers.

SPECIAL EDITION GAMES REMAIN INTACT!
The Commissioner Birthday Classic and Turkey Bowl remain on the schedule. Game Notes will also automatically appear on the Fan Portal when published.

WEEKS 1–7 ARE UNCHANGED!
All previously completed games and official results remain intact.

THE ROAD TO THE TMFL PLAYOFFS JUST GOT MORE INTERESTING!

The revised schedule is available now on the TMFL Fan Portal.

NEW SCHEDULE. NEW RIVALRIES. SAME GOAL: THE TMFL CHAMPIONSHIP.

articles.title: MAJOR 2026 SCHEDULE OVERHAUL!
articles.body:
TMFL BREAKING NEWS: MAJOR 2026 SCHEDULE OVERHAUL!

The TMFL has officially completed a major restructuring of the remainder of the 2026 regular season!

With divisional rivalries, a revamped primetime lineup, and a completely redistributed bye-week schedule, the road to the TMFL Championship just got a whole lot more interesting.

RESTRUCTURED REGULAR-SEASON SCHEDULE

All games beginning in Week 8 have been reorganized to create a more balanced and competitive season. Weeks 1–7 and all completed results remain unchanged.

DIVISIONAL RIVALRIES START IN WEEK 8!

Previously, all 96 divisional matchups were scheduled for Weeks 13–18. Those games are now spread throughout Weeks 8–18, bringing crucial division battles into the playoff picture much earlier!

PRIMETIME FOOTBALL GETS A MAKEOVER!

The TMFL has revamped its future TNF, FNF, Saturday, SNF, and MNF lineups!

Broadcast assignments now prioritize teams that have not previously appeared in the same primetime slot, bringing fresh matchups and more television exposure across the league.

NEW PRIMETIME HIGHLIGHTS:
- Week 8 TNF: Raiders @ Cardinals
- Week 8 MNF: Titans @ Texans
- Week 9 SNF: 49ers @ Chargers
- Week 13 FNF: Chiefs @ Broncos
- Week 14 MNF: Cardinals @ Rams
- Week 18 SNF: Jets @ Patriots

BYE WEEKS REDISTRIBUTED!

Every team's bye week is now scheduled before Week 16!

Weeks 8–14 feature four teams on bye each week, with the remaining two teams resting in Week 15.

WEEKS 16, 17, AND 18 WILL FEATURE ALL 32 TEAMS IN ACTION!

UPDATED DIVISION TIEBREAKERS

Division winning percentage is now the first tiebreaker between teams with identical overall winning percentages, making every divisional matchup even more important.

SPECIAL EDITION GAMES PRESERVED!

The Commissioner Birthday Classic and Turkey Bowl remain intact, and published Game Notes will appear directly on the Fan Portal.

THE FINAL STRETCH IS SET. THE RIVALRIES ARE HEATING UP. AND THE ROAD TO THE PLAYOFFS JUST GOT REAL.

Check out the newly updated schedule on the official TMFL Fan Portal!

32 TEAMS. 18 WEEKS. ONE TMFL CHAMPION.
